stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.6-27B, a Dense Model That Outperforms Its Own 397B MoE on Coding Benchmarks

key_facts.fact: Qwen3.6-27B is a 27-billion-parameter dense open-weight model under Apache 2.0 license, the first dense variant in the Qwen 3.6 family.
On SWE-bench Verified the model scores 77.2%, surpassing the much larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MoE (which scored lower) and approaching Claude 4.5 Opus's 80.9%.
On Terminal-Bench 2.0, Qwen3.6-27B scores 59.3, matching Claude 4.5 Opus exactly and far exceeding the 35B MoE sibling's 51.5.
The model uses a hybrid architecture blending Gated DeltaNet linear attention with traditional self-attention, supporting 262K native context (extendable to 1M tokens via YaRN).
It introduces a Thinking Preservation mechanism that keeps prior chain-of-thought across turns so the model doesn't re-derive scratch work each tool round.
On reasoning benchmarks GPQA Diamond reaches 87.8, AIME 2026 hits 94.1, and LiveCodeBench v6 scores 83.9.

stories.headline: China's 360 Digital Security Uses AI Agent to Discover ~1,000 Unknown Software Vulnerabilities

key_facts.fact: 360 Digital Security Group developed an AI-powered 'Vulnerability Discovery Agent' that uncovered approximately 1,000 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including in Microsoft Office and OpenClaw.

The AI agent used a combination of LLM reasoning, symbolic execution, and reinforcement learning to explore software behavior, finding flaws in memory handling, input validation, and privilege escalation over a six-month testing window.

The findings were detailed in a report by Natto Thoughts, a research group focused on Chinese cybersecurity, positioning 360 as a competitor to Anthropic's Mythos in AI-driven vulnerability discovery.
360 says the agent operates under strict ethical constraints: no live exploitation, no data exfiltration, and testing conducted in isolated, air-gapped environments.
The system reduces vulnerability detection time from weeks to hours, operating continuously and autonomously unlike traditional penetration testing.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Seeks $20B+ Valuation in First Outside Funding Round as Tencent and Alibaba Vie to Invest

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek is in talks with Tencent and Alibaba for its first-ever external funding round, targeting a valuation of more than $20 billion.
The target valuation doubled from initial discussions last week of at least $10 billion, as investor interest surged; the company is seeking to raise at least $300 million.
DeepSeek has relied entirely on backing from parent company High-Flyer Capital Management until now, with its models fully open-source and consumer chatbot free, generating no substantial revenue.
The fundraise comes as DeepSeek faces talent departures (core researcher Luo Fuli joined Xiaomi's MiMo team) and delays to its flagship V4 model originally planned for February.
Some US venture capital firms are cautious about investing because DeepSeek is a Chinese startup, while competitors MiniMax and Zhipu have already gone public in Hong Kong.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Denali's Avlayah, First Biologic Designed to Cross Blood-Brain Barrier, for Hunter Syndrome

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Avlayah (tividenofusp alfa-eknm), the first FDA-approved biologic specifically designed to cross the blood-brain barrier, for treatment of neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome (MPS II).

In the Phase I/II clinical trial, Avlayah demonstrated a 91% reduction in cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate (CSF HS) levels from baseline by week 24; 93% of patients (41 of 44) had CSF HS levels within the range of individuals without Hunter syndrome.

The approval validates Denali's TransportVehicle platform for delivering biologic medicines across the blood-brain barrier, potentially applicable to a wide range of neurodegenerative diseases and lysosomal storage disorders.

Hunter syndrome affects approximately 1 in 100,000 to 170,000 male births; existing therapies like Elaprase cannot reach the brain. Avlayah is the first therapeutic innovation for the community in nearly 20 years.

Continued approval may be contingent upon verification of clinical benefit in the Phase II/III COMPASS confirmatory trial, currently enrolling participants in North America, South America, and Europe.

stories.headline: EU Launches AccelerateEU Strategy to Slash Fossil Fuel Dependence After €24B Iran War Energy Shock

key_facts.fact: The European Commission launched AccelerateEU, a new strategy to reduce fossil fuel dependence and shield the bloc from energy price shocks; the EU has spent an additional €24 billion on energy imports since the Iran war escalation without receiving any extra energy.

The Commission will avoid major market interventions like gas price caps or windfall taxes for now; instead it plans to curb EU tax rules to favour electricity over oil and gas, and make it easier for governments to cut industrial electricity taxes to zero.

EU energy commissioner Dan Jørgensen warned the disruption is costing Europe around €500 million per day; the Commission will present an Electrification Action Plan by summer with a binding electrification target.

The EU produced 71% of its electricity from low-carbon sources (renewables + nuclear) in 2025, up from ~60% in 2022, which analysts say makes the electricity price shock smaller than in 2022 despite the oil shock potentially being worse.
Von der Leyen said: 'We must accelerate the shift to homegrown, clean energies. This will give us energy independence and security, and mean we are better able to weather geopolitical storms.'

stories.headline: Germany Unveils First-Ever Military Strategy, Aims to Be Europe's Strongest Conventional Army by 2029

key_facts.fact: Germany's Chief of Defence General Carsten Breuer signed the Bundeswehr's first Military Strategy on April 22, forming the Overall Concept for Military Defence; the full document is classified.
The strategy targets 460,000 total soldiers (260,000 active, 200,000 reserve) by mid-2030s, with an interim milestone of 204,000 active soldiers by 2029, up from ~186,000 today.
Russia is identified as the 'greatest and most direct threat' to German and transatlantic security; the strategy states 'Russia is creating the conditions for a military attack on NATO countries.'

Priority capabilities include air defence, long-range precision strikes across all domains, territorial missile defence, and AI integration; the strategy introduces a 'One-Theatre-Approach' connecting domains.
Defence Minister Pistorius said: 'Our ambition is and must be to be Europe's strongest conventional military,' noting that AI and automation will impact troop planning and qualifications.

stories.headline: Iran Fires on 3 Ships in Strait of Hormuz and Seizes 2 as US Blockade and Ceasefire Both Continue

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired on three commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz on April 22 and seized two of them (MSC Francesca and Epaminondas), intensifying its assault on shipping in the waterway.

The attacks came hours after Trump extended the ceasefire while maintaining the US naval blockade; Treasury Secretary Bessent said Kharg Island storage will soon be full and Iranian oil wells will be shut in.

Brent crude briefly surpassed $100/barrel, a 35% increase from prewar levels; the standoff has choked off nearly all exports through the strait where 20% of the world's traded oil passes in peacetime.
Iran refused to send a delegation to a second round of peace talks in Pakistan; its chief negotiator said a ceasefire 'only makes sense' if not violated by the US blockade.
The US has turned back 31 vessels since its blockade began on April 13; there have been more than 30 attacks on ships in the Mideast since the war started February 28.
Panama condemned the 'illegal seizure' of the Panama-flagged MSC Francesca, calling it a serious attack on maritime security; the White House said seizures didn't violate ceasefire terms.

stories.headline: Microsoft Commits AU$25B ($18B) to Australian AI Infrastructure by 2029, Its Largest Investment There

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will invest AU$25 billion (US$18 billion) in capital and operational expenditure in Australia by end of 2029, its largest-ever investment in the country.
The investment will expand Microsoft's Azure AI supercomputing and cloud infrastructure, increasing its Australian footprint by more than 140% by end of 2029.
Announced by Satya Nadella alongside PM Anthony Albanese during Microsoft's AI Tour in Sydney, the deal includes training 3 million Australians in AI skills by 2028.
The deal builds on a prior AU$5B commitment from October 2023. Microsoft currently operates 29 datacenter sites across three Azure regions in Australia.
Australia has also received AI infrastructure pledges from AWS (AU$20B) and OpenAI (AU$7B), as Canberra positions itself as a key Asia-Pacific AI hub.

stories.headline: Lutnick Says No Nvidia H200 Chips Sold to China Yet, Beijing Hasn't Approved Purchases

key_facts.fact: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told the Senate Appropriations Committee that Nvidia's H200 chips have not yet been sold to Chinese companies.
Lutnick said the Chinese government has not approved the purchases, citing Beijing's focus on investing in its domestic semiconductor industry.
The Trump administration approved H200 exports to China after the US-China summit in October, but deliveries have been stalled by disagreements on conditions on both sides.
Lutnick emphasized 'The United States will not sell its best semiconductors to China under any circumstances,' noting Blackwell chips are not being sold at all.
Lutnick also appeared to back away from reimposing the 'affiliates rule' restricting tech exports to thousands of Chinese companies, saying it's part of the broader trade deal balance.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Free ChatGPT for Clinicians With Frontier Models and HealthBench Professional

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for verified US physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and pharmacists, offering access to frontier models for clinical workflows.

The tool includes trusted clinical search citing millions of peer-reviewed sources, deep journal research that compiles cited reports in minutes, and skills for repeatable workflows like referral letters and prior authorizations.
Physician advisors reviewed 6,924 conversations and deemed 99.6% of responses safe and accurate; HIPAA support is available through a Business Associate Agreement.
OpenAI also launched HealthBench Professional, an open benchmark for evaluating AI on real clinician tasks; GPT-5.4 in the Clinicians workspace outperformed other models and human physicians.
A 2026 AMA survey found 72% of physicians now use AI in clinical practice, up from 48% the prior year, with weekly usage more than doubled.
Clinical research activities can earn CME credits automatically, and OpenAI plans to expand access internationally through the Better Evidence Network.

stories.headline: OpenAI Releases Privacy Filter, an Open-Weight Model for PII Detection With 1.5B Parameters

key_facts.fact: Privacy Filter is an open-weight model with 1.5 billion total parameters and 50 million active parameters, released under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face and GitHub.
The model processes up to 128,000 tokens in a single forward pass and is small enough to run on a standard laptop or in a web browser.
It uses a sparse MoE bidirectional token-classification architecture (described as a 'Mixture of BERTs') derived from the gpt-oss family.
The model scored 96% on the PII-Masking-300k benchmark out of the box, rising to 97.43% with a corrected version of the test.
It detects eight PII categories: names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, URLs, dates, account numbers, and secrets like passwords and API keys.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Workspace Agents in ChatGPT, Replacing Custom GPTs With Codex-Powered Automation

key_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced workspace agents in ChatGPT, Codex-powered shared agents that can handle complex, multi-step, long-running workflows across connected tools like Slack, Salesforce, and Notion.
Workspace agents run in the cloud and continue working even when users are offline, and are designed to be shared within an organization.
The feature is available as a research preview for ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Teachers plans, free until May 6 when credit-based pricing begins.
OpenAI will make it possible to convert existing custom GPTs directly into workspace agents in the future.
Early adopter Rippling reports 70% time savings on recurring sales workflows, reducing manual effort from 5-6 hours/week to background automation.

stories.headline: Samsung Union Rally Draws 30,000+ Workers Demanding 15% of AI Chip Profits, Threatens 18-Day Strike

key_facts.fact: Police estimated 30,000 attendees (organizers said 39,000-40,000) at the rally outside Samsung's Pyeongtaek semiconductor complex — the largest union rally in Samsung's history.
The union demands 15% of operating profit be allocated to chip-division employees; the total would exceed 40 trillion won ($27B), or more than $400,000 per worker on average.
Workers threaten an 18-day general strike starting May 21 if demands are not met; this could delay chip deliveries to customers and further push up memory prices.

The core grievance is a massive bonus gap with rival SK Hynix: a Samsung chip worker with a ₩76M base salary reportedly received ₩38M in bonuses for 2025, less than one-third what an SK Hynix employee with similar pay would get.

Union membership has surged past 90,000, representing over 70% of Samsung's South Korean workforce; management proposed 10% of operating profit for performance pay and a 6.2% wage increase but rejected abolishing the bonus cap.

stories.headline: 37,000 Samsung Workers Rally at Pyeongtaek Chip Campus, Threaten 18-Day Strike Over Bonus Demands

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics' labor union rallied up to 37,000-40,000 workers at the Pyeongtaek semiconductor campus on April 23, the union's largest show of force to date.
The union demands 15% of annual operating profit as performance bonuses with no cap. With Samsung's projected full-year operating profit at ~306 trillion won, that implies a ~45 trillion won payout.
The union has threatened an 18-day walkout from May 21 through June 7 if negotiations fail, which it claims would cost Samsung more than 1 trillion won ($676M) per day.

A small group of retail shareholders staged a counterdemonstration, with one organizer calling the union's demands 'no different from a predatory creditor's,' citing that the 45T won demand dwarfs the 11.1T won Samsung paid in dividends last year.
Union membership has tripled since Samsung's first worker walkout in 2024 to over 90,000 members, representing more than 70% of South Korean staff. Workers cite a pay gap with rival SK Hynix.
Samsung filed for a court injunction to block occupation of production lines. The rally came hours after SK Hynix posted record earnings, sharpening comparisons.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Posts Record Q1: Revenue Tops 50T Won for First Time, 72% Operating Margin Surpasses Nvidia

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix reported Q1 operating profit of 37.61 trillion won ($27.8B), five times higher than a year earlier, and record revenue of 52.58 trillion won ($38.9B), up 198% YoY — the first time quarterly revenue surpassed 50 trillion won.
Operating margin reached 72%, surpassing Nvidia's semiconductor industry peak of 65% (Q4 2025) and TSMC's 58.1% (Q1 2026), an unprecedented level for an asset-heavy memory manufacturer.
The average price of DRAM used in HBM jumped to $13/unit at end of Q1, ten times the $1.35 of a year earlier; SK Hynix held a 57% share of the HBM market.
SK Hynix said HBM demand will exceed its production capacity for the next three years; the company plans to ship HBM4E samples in H2 2026 and begin mass production in 2027.
SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won reportedly said in March that the global chip wafer shortage is likely to persist until 2030, with a projected shortfall exceeding 20%.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Posts Record Q1 With 72% Operating Margin as HBM Demand Exceeds Supply for 3 Years

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix reported Q1 revenue of 52.58 trillion won ($38.9B), up 198% YoY, the first time quarterly revenue surpassed 50 trillion won.
Operating profit reached a record 37.61 trillion won ($27.8B), up 405% YoY, with an operating margin of 72%, surpassing both Samsung Electronics (43%) and major Big Tech companies.
Net profit reached 40.35 trillion won ($29.8B), including approximately 14 trillion won in non-operating income from foreign exchange gains and valuation gains.
SK Hynix said HBM demand will exceed its production capacity for the next three years and announced plans to ship HBM4E samples in H2 2026, with mass production in 2027.
DRAM ASP rose mid-60% range QoQ, NAND ASP rose mid-70% range QoQ; average HBM DRAM price jumped to $13, ten times the $1.35 of a year earlier.
Cash and equivalents reached 54.3 trillion won, up 19.4 trillion won QoQ, with net cash of 35 trillion won after borrowings fell to 19.3 trillion won.

stories.headline: Tencent Releases Hy3-Preview, First Flagship AI Model Under Former OpenAI Researcher Yao Shunyu

key_facts.fact: Tencent released and open-sourced Hy3-preview (Hunyuan 3.0 Preview), a MoE language model with 295B total parameters, 21B activated parameters, and 256K max context length.
The model is smaller than Tencent's previous flagship HY 2.0 (400B+ parameters), reflecting a focus on balancing performance and cost-effectiveness rather than pursuing massive scale.
It is the first model since former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu joined Tencent as Chief AI Scientist; training began in late January 2026 and took less than three months.
On SWE-Bench coding benchmarks, Hy3-preview scored 74.4%, up from Hy2's 53.0%, a more than 40% improvement in coding capability.
Tencent says agentic capabilities were one of the most significantly improved areas; the model has been deployed in Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, and other internal Tencent products.
Yao Shunyu stated Hy3-preview is the first step in reconstructing the Hunyuan large model, and a larger model is already in development.

stories.headline: Tesla Becomes Intel's First Major 14A Customer for Terafab AI Chip Manufacturing Complex

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk said during Tesla's Q1 earnings call that Tesla plans to use Intel's 14A process for chips at the Terafab AI complex in Austin, making Tesla the first major external customer for the node.
Musk said '14A seems like the right move' and that by the time Terafab scales up, the technology should be 'fairly mature or ready for prime time.'
Terafab is designed to deliver up to one terawatt of AI compute annually, roughly double the current total generated across the US, with construction alone estimated at $25 billion.
Intel's 14A process is expected to reach production readiness in 2027, with early PDK versions already rolling out to external customers this year.
Tesla CFO said the company expects over $25 billion in capex this year. SpaceX will be responsible for high-volume chip manufacturing at TeraFab.

stories.headline: Texas Instruments Q1 Revenue Jumps 19% to $4.83B as Data Center Nearly Doubles, Guides Q2 Above Street

key_facts.fact: TI reported Q1 revenue of $4.83B, up 19% YoY, beating analyst estimates of $4.53B by 6.6%. EPS of $1.68 beat estimates of $1.36 by 23.1%.
Data Center revenue nearly doubled YoY (~90% growth), while Industrial revenue rose over 30% YoY with broad-based gains across sectors and regions.
Q2 revenue guidance of $5.0B-$5.4B ($5.2B midpoint) was 7.1% above analyst estimates of $4.86B. Q2 EPS guidance of $1.77-$2.05 also beat consensus.
Operating margin expanded to 37.5% from 32.5% a year earlier. Trailing 12-month free cash flow surged 154% YoY to $4.35B.
CEO Ilan called it 'the first quarter where we saw the broad market starting to wake up again after a long hibernation,' marking 8 consecutive quarters of sequential growth.

stories.headline: TSMC Unveils Roadmap Through 2029 With A12 and A13 Nodes, Skips ASML's High-NA EUV Through Decade

key_facts.fact: TSMC revealed A13 (1.3nm) and A12 (1.2nm) process nodes at its 2026 North American Technology Symposium, both targeted for production in 2029. A13 offers 6% area savings over A14 with full backward compatibility.
TSMC will not use ASML's high-NA EUV machines (costing €350M+ each) for any production nodes through 2029, choosing to maximize current EUV equipment instead.
TSMC is adopting a dual-track strategy: new client/mobile nodes every year, and AI/HPC nodes with backside power delivery every two years. A16 slipped to 2027.
A 14-reticle size CoWoS package capable of integrating 10 large compute dies and 20 HBM stacks is slated for production in 2028, with beyond-14-reticle and 40-reticle SoW-X in 2029.
TSMC SVP Kevin Zhang confirmed the company plans to open a CoWoS and 3D-IC advanced chip packaging plant in Arizona by 2029, with construction already underway.
The decision contrasts with Intel, which has installed ASML's High-NA EUV system and expects risk production in 2027, and Samsung, which received its first High-NA scanner in late 2025.

stories.headline: Wall Street's 6 Largest Banks Cut 15,000 Jobs in Q1 Citing AI While Posting $47B in Combined Profit

key_facts.fact: The six largest Wall Street banks — JPMorgan Chase, Citi, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Wells Fargo — collectively eliminated 15,000 positions in Q1 2026 while posting combined profits of $47 billion, an 18% increase YoY.

Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan reversed his earlier assurance that AI posed no threat to jobs, announcing the bank shed 1,000 positions through attrition by 'eliminating work and applying technology.'
Citi committed to reducing its workforce by 20,000 employees through what it calls a 'productivity and efficiency journey,' using AI software from Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI.
AI is being deployed across banking to automate paperwork compliance, account opening approvals, invoice generation, legal document review, and organization of sensitive customer data.

Some 80,000 tech workers were laid off in Q1 2026, with 47.9% attributed to AI and automation according to Nikkei Asia; even Sam Altman admitted there is 'AI washing' where companies blame AI for layoffs they planned anyway.
